Comprehensive Guide to Spring Valley Municipal Court

Overview of Spring Valley Municipal Court

The Spring Valley Municipal Court is located in Houston, within the Spring Valley Village City Park. This court falls under the 9th and 2nd Judicial Departments and handles various cases such as C-class misdemeanors, city ordinance violations, traffic matters, small claims, eviction, and civil and criminal cases within corporate city limits. Only fines are imposed as penalties. The court’s mission is to provide a fair and impartial forum of justice, ensuring all citizens are treated equally regardless of financial status, religion, or other factors. Note that children, family, and friends are not permitted in the courtroom.

Key Information:

  • Address: 1025 Campbell Rd, Houston, TX 77055, United States
  • Phone: 713-465-0333
  • Email: municipalcourt@springvalleytx.com
  • Website: Spring Valley Municipal Court

Working Hours:

  • Monday to Friday: 7:30 AM – 4:30 PM
  • Saturday and Sunday: Closed

Key Personnel:

  • Judges:
    • Judge James Smith
    • Judge John J. Klevenhagen III
    • Judge Stephan Smith Andrews
  • Chief Prosecutor: Bob Richter (Phone: 713-465-8308)
  • Court Administrator: Ronaldo Rodriguez

Services Provided by Spring Valley Municipal Court

Types of Cases Handled

  • Traffic Violations: Speeding, accidents, and other vehicle-related offenses.
  • City Ordinance Violations: Addressing infractions within corporate city limits.
  • Small Claims and Eviction Cases: Civil disputes and tenant-landlord disagreements.
  • Criminal Cases: Handling misdemeanors punishable by fines only.

Court Divisions

The court is divided into the following divisions:

  • Civil Division: Handles small claims and evictions.
  • Criminal Division: Addresses misdemeanors and ordinance violations.
  • Traffic Division: Resolves vehicle-related offenses and violations.

How to Navigate Court Procedures

Case Search

To find case information, search online by:

  1. Name
  2. Citation Number
  3. Driver’s License Number
  4. Vehicle Information Some information may require a formal request for access.

Payment Options

Fines can be paid through the following methods:

  1. In-Person: Pay via cash, check, or card at the court office. Credit card payments require a photo ID and incur a 5% service fee.
  2. Online: Visit Spring Valley Online Payments.
  3. Mail: Send a certified check with the citation number to the court address.
  4. Phone: Call 888-291-1724 to make a payment.

Warrants

A warrant is issued if fines or ticket fees are not paid by the due date, or if court appearances are missed when mandatory. Once issued, the warrant is shared with law enforcement agencies, potentially leading to arrest.

Special Circumstances

Juvenile Cases

For individuals under 16, a court appearance with parents or guardians is mandatory. Failure to appear results in a notification to the Texas Department of Public Safety, preventing the juvenile from obtaining a driver’s license. Parents may face misdemeanor charges if they fail to attend.

Driver’s Safety Course

Eligibility for taking the course includes:

  1. Permission from the court.
  2. No similar course taken in the past 12 months.
  3. Submission of a plea of “No Contest” or “Guilty.”
  4. Presentation of a valid Texas Driver’s License and insurance policy.
  5. Payment of $144 (or $169 if the offense occurred in a school zone). Required documents include:
  • Insurance card showing the defendant’s name.
  • Valid Texas Driver’s License. These documents must be submitted in person at the court clerk’s window.

Plea of Not Guilty

To enter a plea of not guilty, complete the “Reset or Not Guilty” form available on the court’s website. Submit the form via email to municipalcourt@springvalleytx.com at least five days before the court date.

Additional Services

Marriage Licenses

Marriage licenses can be obtained at the clerk’s office. Fees range from $35 to $65, with copies costing $14. Requirements:

  • Applicants must be at least 18 years old.
  • Parental or guardian consent is required for those aged 16 or 17.
  • A valid photo ID and birth certificate must be provided. The license is valid for three months, and ceremonies can be held at the court.

Legal Resources

  • Driver’s License Holds or Surcharges: Contact the Department of Public Safety at 512-424-2600.
  • Driving Records: Order a 3A driving record online or by mail. Visit the Texas DPS Driver Records page for details.
  • Mailing Address for Records: Texas Department of Public Safety, PO Box 149008, Austin, TX 78714-9008.

Frequently Asked Questions

What types of cases are heard at the Spring Valley Municipal Court?

The court handles traffic violations, misdemeanors, city ordinance violations, and small claims cases.

How can I pay my fine?

Payments can be made in person, online, via mail, or over the phone.

Can I appeal a decision?

Yes, appeals can be filed following court procedures.
